note: Behavioral eval set for craft-ops/infrastructure-authoring. Each prompt asks for a narrated plan (not files) so it can be graded from text; assertions guard the domain rules the authoring skill was validated on, plus craft-ops core 2 (proven by running, no default unit-test suite for glue).

evals.discriminates: structural IaC rules plus plan/apply/re-plan as the proof
evals.prompt: Our infrastructure design note for the orders service on AWS calls for: a VPC with public/private/data subnets, a Postgres RDS instance, an S3 bucket for receipts, and an ECS Fargate service running the API. Terraform. Author it. Don't write files — narrate the units/modules you'd create, their order, and exactly how you'd verify the result before calling it done.
assertions: Network foundation is its own unit applied first; others receive its IDs as inputs
Durable resources (RDS, S3) are in their own unit(s), never co-located with the compute (ECS) unit; compute receives their identifiers as inputs
Durable resources sit in an isolated data segment reachable by default only from compute
Remote, locked state; no secrets in code or state (e.g. managed master password / secret manager)
Verification: validate, plan, READ the plan checking for destroy/replace of durable resources, apply to a sandbox, then a second plan showing no changes
Does NOT propose unit tests that mock the provider / restate resource definitions
